cover letter

01. PLEASE READ THE FOLLOWING STATEMENT CAREFULLY: Please answer all supplemental questions truthfully, accurately, and completely. You are not expected to select the highest response level for each question in order to qualify. Your application and supplemental responses will be reviewed to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for this position. Your responses may also be evaluated as part of a Training and Experience (T&E) assessment to determine the extent of your relevant education, training, and experience. Responses such as “see resume,” “see application,” or similar references will not be accepted in place of a complete response. Incomplete responses may not receive credit and may result in disqualification from the examination process. You are required to answer all supplemental questions as truthfully and accurately as possible. Information provided in your responses is subject to verification and must be supported by the education, training, certifications, and experience listed in your application. Please do not use generative artificial intelligence (AI) to prepare your responses to narrative supplemental questions. Any intentional misrepresentation, falsification, or significant exaggeration of your qualifications may result in disqualification from the examination process and may affect eligibility for future employment opportunities with the District. Select “Yes” if you have read, understood, and agree to the statements above. Select “No” if you have read and understood the statements above but do not agree and wish to withdraw your application from consideration. Options: Yes | No

02. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some high school | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college, but less than 60 units | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree
03. Please indicate the field in which you obtained your degree. If you do not possess a degree, list "n/a".

04. How many years of progressively responsible experience do you have in financial management within a public agency, including accounting, budgeting, and fiscal administration? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year | 1 year but less than 2 years | 2 years but less than 3 years | 3 years but less than 4 years | 4 years but less than 5 years | 5years but less than 6 years | 6 or more years

05. Describe your experience developing a budget, preparing interim financial reports, and completing year-end closing. In your response, include: a) Your specific role in each activity (for example, lead, preparer, or support) b) The size of the budget(s), in dollars c) How you communicated budget information and to whom d) Your job title, the organization, and the dates you held the position

06. Describe a time when you made a difficult financial decision that significantly affected your organization. In your response, explain: a) The situation and why the decision was difficult b) How you gathered and analyzed information c) How you evaluated the potential impact on the organization d) What resources you identified and used (for example, staff, data, or outside expertise) e) The decision you made and the outcome

07. Describe your experience performing technical accounting work in each of the following areas: general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, revenue, grants, special funds, fixed assets, and payroll. For each area, include: a) Your specific role (for example, lead, preparer, reviewer, or support) b) The types of tasks you performed c) Your job title, the organization, and the dates you held the position If you have no experience in this area, list "n/a".

08. Describe your experience with annual financial audits and the preparation of annual financial reports or statements, such as an Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR). In your response, include: a) Your specific role (for example, lead, preparer, reviewer, or support) b) The tasks you performed (for example, preparing schedules, reconciling accounts, responding to auditor requests, or drafting statements or notes) c) The size or type of organization d) Your job title, the organization, and the dates you held the position If you have no experience in this area, list "n/a".

09. How many years of experience do you possess in a supervisory or management capacity, specifically overseeing employees responsible for professional, technical, or administrative fiscal functions? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year | 1 year but less than 2 years | 2 years but less than 3 years | 3 years but less than 4 years | 4 years but less than 5 years | 5 years but less than 6 years | 6 or more years

10. Please describe your supervisory or management experience overseeing employees responsible for fiscal functions such as accounting, budgeting, payroll, purchasing, accounts payable, financial reporting, or related activities. For each related experience, please include: a) Your job title(s) b) Name of the organization(s) c) Number of direct and indirect reports d) Job titles or classifications of employees supervised e) Your responsibilities for assigning and reviewing work, training, evaluating performance, hiring or selection, corrective or disciplinary action, and other supervisory functions If you have no experience in this area, list "n/a".

Plans, organizes, directs, and participates in the functions and activities of the fiscal services unit, including budget preparation and control, payroll preparation, purchasing, and record maintenance, and systems and processes pertaining to the proper disbursement of funds, assure compliance with applicable laws, codes, rules and regulations.
Plans, organizes, prepares, and presents periodic financial statements outlining the district's income and expenditure position for all funds.
Performs fiscal analyses and audits and provides preliminary budget estimates and projections.
Oversees the calculation and projection of the District’s apportionments, especially calculations related to enrollment, attendance and unduplicated pupil count.
Counsels, confers with, and advises district and site personnel regarding budget-related matters and issues, and aids in determining alternative fiscal problem solutions.
Reviews, monitors, and controls categorical budgets and major account expenditures, and alerts appropriate management personnel before accounts reach a predetermined expenditure limit.

Directs and performs financial and budget master planning process, including near-, mid-, and long-range planning, determination of human and monetary resource needs, and the establishment of fiscal goals and objectives.
Oversees and executes the planning, organizing, and development of fiscal policies, regulations, and operational guidelines.
Plans, develops, and implements procedures pertaining to the investment of excess district funds.
Serves as a liaison to external auditors and analyzes, evaluates, and interprets audit reports to appropriate levels of management.
Plans, develops, and implements fiscal and record management procedures to ensure adherence to an effective and efficient operational mode.
Reviews, monitors, and evaluates the performance of subordinates and assists them in the resolution of unusual or unforeseen problems and concerns.
Supervises, trains, and evaluates assigned personnel.
Aids fiscal service personnel in resolving rights disputes, which may include conducting hearing processes.

May serve as a member or a resource to the District’s collective bargaining team; prepare fiscal information for collective bargaining activities; maintain confidentiality regarding issues related to negotiations and other collective bargaining matters.

Attends and participates in a variety of meetings, workshops, conferences and training to maintain current knowledge of emerging trends; makes presentations regarding District financial objectives, plans and achievements to groups and committees.

Coordinates the preparation and administration of grant applications and awarded funds by overseeing necessary documentation, tracking expenditures, and verifying compliance to secure external funding and ensure adherence to regulatory standards.
May perform the more technical and responsible fiscal services functions.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Principles, methods, procedures, and trends pertaining to the management of budget, accounting, and fiscally related processes.
Effectively and efficiently coordinate, manage, and direct the district fiscal programs and processes.
Audit, fiscal control, and research process methods, procedures, and strategies.
Analyze financial data and perform comprehensive audits of funds and accounts
Principles, trends, techniques, and strategies of modern organization management and supervision.
Develop and implement effective budget, accounting, and fiscal control procedures
Legal mandates, policies, regulations, and guidelines pertaining to educational fiscal management processes.
Lead and develop fiscal services personnel through effective supervision and training
Government accounting standards and practices applicable to school districts
Build and maintain cooperative relationships with administrators, staff, and external agencies
California school finance, attendance accounting, and apportionment processes
Exercise sound judgment in financial decision-making
Financial reporting requirements for educational agencies
Adapt fiscal operations to meet changing regulatory requirements
Principles of investment and cash flow management
Present financial information effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences
Computerized financial systems and related software applications
Maintain confidentiality with sensitive fiscal and personnel information
Grant management and compliance requirements
Model communications and interactions that respect and include all individuals and their languages, abilities, religions, and cultures
Collective bargaining processes and fiscal implications
Budget development and multi-year forecasting methodologies
Fundamental concepts of employment laws, codes, and regulations, including EEO, FLSA, FMLA, and Cal/OSHA
Communicate complex financial information clearly both verbally and in writing
Work independently with minimal oversight while maintaining accountability
Demonstrate the highest standards of fiscal ethics, professional integrity, and accountability in all aspects of financial management
